scope: Theorem 7.1 (The Abelian clamp) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 82. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the finite problem P and a fixed upper bound on total topological charge, the metrics and fixed line connections of Theorem 6.1 can be chosen with all artificial isolation lengths finite so that the following assertions hold simultaneously, including at every genuine face. (i) On an R or S component containing a positive bridge, either u = 0, or there is a nonempty subset I of its adjacent whole sides such that sign(u)zI ≤ 0 (R), sign(u)zI < |λI| (S). (7.4) (ii) No R component contains an outside cap. For each fixed old cap W, cut at its rational seams and before its extra blow-up, there is a constant CW such that an S component satisfies v2 W ≤ CW , (ΛW + vW )2 ≤ CW . (7.5) The constant depends only on W, its fixed line data, metric and boundary collars. It is independent of the number of added intervals and of the new exceptional evaluations. (iii) On an actually separated Ni the fixed background is harmonic and anti-self-dual, and the metric has positive scalar curvature. The complementary metrics and backgrounds agree for the two bit choices differing by the class supported on Ni. One may first choose a positive bound for the ordinary Floer-gradient perturbations on the finite Y seams and then take those seams to any sufficiently large finite gluing lengths. Once those lengths have been chosen, further compatible perturbations may be made sufficiently small, including in total squared L2 cost on the seams. Precise quantifiers are given in Corollary 7.10. The charge assumption concerns the sum over all retained fields and nonnegative ideal losses. No sign assumption is made on the charge of an arbitrary PU(2) component.
